{"id": "07963701-f98c-4a1e-b4bb-ba3b9cb8dc82", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is general AWS knowledge rather than something tied to a specific function, so I can answer directly: Lambda's default timeout is 3 seconds, and it can be increased up to a maximum of 900 seconds (15 minutes) via configuration.\n\n"}]}

{"id": "04238fe1-62fb-4006-b2cd-c60773209ffc", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "## Why it times out at 3 seconds

3 seconds is the **default Lambda timeout**. If you never set a timeout, Lambda stops the invocation at 3 seconds. You'll see `Task timed out after 3.00 seconds` in the function's logs.

Raising the limit only helps if the function really needs more time. If it's slow because of something else, a longer timeout just delays the failure. Common causes:

- **Cold starts.** Large packages, heavy imports, or VPC-attached functions can use up much of the 3 seconds before your handler runs.
- **Slow downstream calls.** Database queries, third-party APIs, or other AWS service calls can be slow.
- **No network path in a VPC.** A function in a VPC with no NAT gateway or VPC endpoint will hang on calls to the internet or to AWS APIs until it times out.
- **Too little memory.** Memory also sets CPU, so a low setting can make CPU-bound work slow.
- **Connection reuse.** Creating a new DB or SDK client on every invocation adds latency.

## How to raise the limit

The maximum is **900 seconds (15 minutes)**.

**Console:** open the function, go to **Configuration → General configuration → Edit**, and change **Timeout**.

**AWS CLI:**
```bash
aws lambda update-function-configuration \
  --function-name my-function \
  --timeout 30
```

**CloudFormation/SAM:**
```yaml
MyFunction:
  Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
  Properties:
    Timeout: 30
```

**Terraform:** set `timeout = 30` on the `aws_lambda_function` resource.

### Things to check alongside it
- **Upstream timeouts.** API Gateway has a 29-second integration timeout by default. An ALB or SQS source has its own limits too. For SQS, set the queue's visibility timeout to at least 6 times the function timeout.
- **Right-size the value.** Set the timeout to a bit above your observed p99 duration, not to the maximum. A runaway invocation then fails fast instead of racking up cost.
- **Test memory.** Increasing memory often shortens duration enough that you don't need a longer timeout.
- **Long-running work.** If it regularly needs more than a few minutes, consider Step Functions, Fargate, or an async/queue-based design.

If you tell me the function name, account, and region, I can look at its current configuration and recent duration metrics to see whether it needs a higher timeout or has a deeper problem.
